newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Eurobourses end higher, dollar in fine form.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Eurobourses end higher, dollar in fine form.

text.p: European bourses closed the week's trading generally firmer, buoyed by strong bonds but curbed by Wall Street's weakness, while the dollar ended steady and poised for gains.
British stocks closed mostly higher on Friday, propelled by strong drug and oil stocks. The FTSE 100 index ended 13.2 points up at 3,946.4 with gainers nearly matching decliners 49 to 46.
Biotechnology major Zeneca powered a rally in drug stocks after U.S. approval for an asthma treatment while Enterprise led a rise in heavily-weighted oil stocks.

Firm gilts helped support shares through much of the session yet a weak Dow opening -- down five points as London closed -- dragged the FTSE off its highs, with strategists saying Wall Street was showing signs of concern about slowing profit growth.

Italian shares closed sharply higher following domestic bonds upwards on optimism over the accord struck on Italy's 1997 financial budget which is aimed at putting Italy on track to join a European single currency, dealers said.
Shares were very much in catch-up mode throughout most of Friday following surging bonds and the rampant lira which hit new 25-months highs in late Thursday trade.
"The deal on the budget has brightened prospects and encouraged investors into Italian stocks," said one dealer.
The all-share Mibtel index ended up 3.09 percent at 10,154 and the Mib30 index was 3.48 percent higher at 15,323.

In Frankfurt, German shares closed bourse floor trade slightly lower on a mild bout of profit-taking following recent moves up towards record-highs, but the underlying tone was helped by continued dollar strength.
DAX futures eased, but were off their lows. The 30-share DAX blue chip index closed 7.51 points lower at 2,659.04 on modest volumes, while the electronically traded IBIS DAX ended down 5.10.

In Paris, French shares closed firm, sustained by continued strength in bond markets, traders said. The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up around three points. In currencies, the dollar ended the European week in fine form, boosted by a broad-based mark retreat and expectations that Japanese interest rates will remain low, analysts said.
Pre-weekend profit-taking took the U.S. currency off its highs against the mark and the yen, but sentiment remained bullish for the dollar.

"I expect the dollar to maintain a fairly favourable tone into the next week," said James McKay, international economist at Paine Webber in London. "It should remain well supported by the market's positive attitude to U.S. fundamentals."
"The point is that the dollar is so well supported on dips, both against the mark and the yen," said a senior dealer at a German bank in London. "I'm confident that it will go higher."
A firm cap for dollar/yen lurks at 111 yen though, which is within a whisker of the two-year high at 111.20, traders said.
Against the mark, the dollar was capped by offers in the mid-1.52 area from funds and European corporates.
The dollar is also likely to be underpinned by the meeting of Group of Seven finance ministers and central bankers in Washington.
The British pound rose against the mark on Friday to hit its highest level this year, boosted by mark weakness and a buoyant gilt market, dealers said Friday.

It eclipsed the July peak of 2.3822 marks to trade at levels not seen since February 1995. It was at 2.3840 by late afternoon. Sterling also traded at three-year highs against the yen above 173 yen, its highest level since April 1993.
CURRENCIES AT 1700 GMT
The dollar was quoted at 1.5235 marks and 110.73 yen, up slightly from late Thursday's European level of 1.5209 marks and 110.40 yen.
STOCK MARKETS CLOSING PRICES
LONDON - The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares ended up 13.2 points at 3,946.4
PARIS - The CAC-40 share index closed up 2.91 points at 2,107.5.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index was down 7.51 points at 2.659.04. The IBIS DAX was down 5.10 at 2,659.86. PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed firmer at $381.15 vs $379.15 on Thursday. Silver ended up four cents at $4.93. Platinum finished down 25 cents at $385.25.
